title: Extract a color from an image

seo.metaTitle: Extract Color From PNG - Keep One Color, Drop The Rest
seo.metaDescription: Keep only the pixels close to a chosen color and make everything else transparent. Free, no upload - the image is processed in your browser.
seo.longDescription: Extract a color keeps only the pixels close to one chosen color and clears everything else — the inverse of removing a color. The result is one flat shape on a transparent background, which is how you pull a single logo color or badge out of a picture and drop it on a page. A tolerance setting decides how far a pixel may sit from the chosen color and still count as it, so a slightly soft edge can be kept or trimmed away. Everything runs in your browser, so the image is never uploaded.
facts: Runs entirely in your browser: no upload, no server, no signup.
Keeps the chosen color and makes everything else transparent.
The eyedropper on the color field samples a pixel straight from the image.
Tolerance pulls in shades near the color: gradients and anti-aliased edges.
Free with no daily limit, no watermark and no account, also for commercial use.
howTo: Drop the image into the source area, or pick a file from your device.
Pick the color you want to keep; the eyedropper on the color field samples a pixel of the image.
Set the tolerance: lower values keep only exact matches, higher values include shades nearby.
Download the result as a transparent PNG, or pick another output format in the Download button.

faq.q: What does the result look like?
faq.a: The pixels close to the chosen color, unchanged, on a fully transparent background. Anything outside the tolerance is cleared, including its own alpha, so the shape has no leftover halo.

faq.q: How do I choose a tolerance?
faq.a: Start low and raise it while the result looks cut off at the edges. Gradients, shadows and anti-aliased edges all sit slightly off the pure color, so a little tolerance usually gives a cleaner shape than none.

faq.q: Is this the same as remove color?
faq.a: It is the opposite operation. Remove Color makes the chosen color transparent and keeps everything else; this tool keeps the chosen color and removes everything else.
No. The pixels are read and the mask is computed in your browser tab, so the file never travels to a server and is not stored.
